raw_response:
I've been farming these 6 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. My father taught me, and I finished primary school — enough to read fertilizer bags and do sums on paper. Most of what I know comes from doing it and watching others. I have 4 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 2 mu in cotton. My youngest son works in Handan and sends some money home, but I still count every yuan. I don't trust outside advice unless I saw it work on someone else's field.

For wheat: I plant improved seed, not the old traditional kind. I switched years ago after Old Wang across the lane got better yield. This year I will put down one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's 25 kilograms of 15-15-15. Then at green-up time in March, I will spread another 25 jin of urea per mu. That works out to about 19 kilograms of nitrogen, 8 kilograms of phosphorus, and 8 kilograms of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, and once when the heads are filling. The well has good water, thank heavens. I will spray pesticide twice, mainly for aphids and rust. I use the rotary tiller before planting — no time for deep ploughing, and the wheat doesn't need it. Last year I got 450 kilograms per mu; this year I expect 470 if the weather holds.

For maize: As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I plant hybrid maize. Everyone uses hybrid now — the yield is just too good to ignore. I will put compound fertilizer in the rows at planting, about 40 jin per mu, then topdress with 30 jin of urea when the plants are knee-high. That is about 20 kilograms of nitrogen, 6 kilograms of phosphorus, and 6 kilograms of potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice — once right after planting if it's dry, and once at tasseling. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer. The rotary tiller runs right after the wheat combine leaves. Last year I got 520 kilograms per mu; I am hoping for 530 this year.

For cotton: My 2 mu of cotton I plant with hybrid seed in late April. Cotton needs more pesticide — there's no way around it with bollworm around here. I will put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, 50 jin, and topdress twice with urea. Total about 15 kilograms of nitrogen, 7 kilograms of phosphorus, and 7 kilograms of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times and spray pesticide four times. I plough the cotton field properly in spring — cotton likes loose, deep soil. Good cotton gives me about 100 kilograms of lint per mu.

Why these numbers? Because this is what I did last year, and last year was decent. A bag of compound fertilizer is over 150 yuan now. For 6 mu I need 8 or 9 bags total, plus urea — that's a lot of money. But I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than too little. Losing yield is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost you absorb. When I am unsure, I do what I did before. I watch Old Zhang and Li the younger — they apply about the same as me. If everyone around you does something, you do something similar. Change is risky.
